title: Central bark shrine (Philip III Arrhidaeus)

claims.text: Within the central sanctuary area known as the Palace of Ma’at.
The surviving two-room shrine belongs to Philip III Arrhidaeus, succeeding Thutmose III’s shrine. Rose granite and a decorated ceiling distinguish the surviving structure.
Thutmose III’s predecessor shrine replaced Hatshepsut’s Red Chapel; the Red Chapel is now reconstructed elsewhere.
Philip’s text claims fidelity to Thutmose III’s shrine. Treat this as a royal claim, not proof that every detail was copied.

caveats: Present access, exact viewpoints and condition have not been field-verified.
